## Current role

Applied AI Architect & GenAI Systems Lead at Accenture Ireland, Dublin (Aug 2025 – present).
Leading design and delivery of production GenAI systems for regulated enterprise clients.

## What I build

I build production GenAI systems for regulated environments:
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with hybrid vector/keyword/graph stacks
- Agentic workflows with human-in-the-loop checkpoints and audit trails
- LLM evaluation and model readiness — capability, reliability, governance behavior, groundedness, security reasoning, cost/latency, failure taxonomy
- Observability and LLMOps — Langfuse, MLflow, quality/safety/cost/latency monitoring
- Security controls — prompt injection defense, sandboxed execution, role-based access control
- AI governance — risk classification, auditability, EU AI Act readiness, policy-to-implementation

## Prior experience

National Science Foundation — Lead Data Scientist / AI Oversight (GS-15), reporting directly to NSF's Chief AI Officer, Sep 2024 – Aug 2025.
Built NSF's first vector and graph database capabilities. Created an initial AI deployment playbook. Co-chaired 100+ member AI Community of Practice.
Note: This work occurred during the early build-out of NSF's Chief AI Officer function and before NSF's later public AI Strategy was drafted and published. I did not author the published strategy.

Accenture Federal Services — Machine Learning Engineer Manager, Jun 2021 – Sep 2024.
Shipped State Department GenAI, Army secured automation, IARPA global geospatial CV. Personally achieved 99.6% ML infrastructure cost reduction on global geospatial platform.

Booz Allen Hamilton — Lead Scientist, DARPA program management. $30M+ in program funds advised.

ODNI / NGA — IC Postdoctoral Researcher. Drone ML, computer vision, CUDA.

## Case studies

- Lock-In, Then Meter (white paper): https://codychampion.bitsandbeakers.com/writing/lock-in-then-meter/
  A build-versus-buy decision brief for AI inference after the flat-rate era. Argues the real hedge against token metering is switchability (an OpenAI-compatible interface, interchangeable open-weight providers, and a frontier model held in reserve), not owning GPUs. Managed open-model inference usually wins on cost; owned hardware only pays past roughly 100B tokens/month with a dedicated platform team. Includes a downloadable PDF, an editable cost model (xlsx), and the model source (Python).
- NSF AI Governance Foundations: https://codychampion.bitsandbeakers.com/case-study-nsf-ai-governance
  Greenfield AI governance, technical review, community, security, and vector/graph architecture inside NSF's Chief AI Officer function. Pre-strategy operating layer for responsible AI adoption across a major U.S. science agency.
- 99.6% ML Inference Cost Reduction for Global Geospatial Workloads: https://codychampion.bitsandbeakers.com/case-study-ml-cost
  Five compounding engineering defects generating $26,200/month rebuilt to $90/month. Personally owned codebase and cloud architecture.
- LLM Evaluation Workbench / Model Readiness Leaderboard: https://codychampion.bitsandbeakers.com/projects/llm-eval-workbench
  Public model-readiness benchmark for regulated enterprise AI using benign synthetic or public-domain scenarios, reviewable artifacts, cost, and latency evidence.
- PAEF: Atomic LLM Evaluation for Contract Compliance: https://codychampion.bitsandbeakers.com/research/paef-contract-compliance
  Multi-contract, multi-model evaluation research comparing atomic microagent checks with monolithic auditing; published on Zenodo in April 2026.
